दंश्: √daṃś or daś (dáśati [746]; dadáṃśa; daśiṣyáti; daṣṭá; daṃṣṭvā́; -dáśya). bite. [cf. δάκνω, ‘bite’; Goth. tahjan, ‘rend, tear.’]
दंष्ट्र: dáṃṣṭra, m. large tooth; tusk; fang. [√daṃś, 1185b.]
दंष्ट्रिन्: daṃṣṭrin, a. having tusks or large teeth. [daṃṣṭra.]
दक्ष्: √dakṣ (dákṣati, -te; dadakṣé; dakṣiṣyáte ). act. suit; mid. be able or dexterous or strong. [cf. dakṣa and dakṣiṇa.]
दक्ष: dákṣa, a. able, dexterous, strong; as m. ability, faculty, strength, power; esp. spiritual power, will; dakṣa and kratu, will and understanding (as faculties of the manas, ‘soul’). [√dakṣ: cf. δεξιός, ‘clever, right,’ and dakṣiṇa.]
दक्षिण: dákṣiṇa, a. 	—1. clever, able; and so 	—2. (as opp. to awkward, gauche), right, of the hand, hasta, e. g. 10211; so pāṇi, 605; foot, pāda, 605; side, pārśva, 10212; 	—3. southern (because in prayer the face is turned eastward: cf. uttara 3), 1058; sc. agni, southern fire, 1023N.; 	—4. as f., dakṣiṇā, sc. go, the able, i. e. fruitful cow, milch cow; milch cow as the customary reward for conducting a sacrifice; then, 	—5. in general, any reward or present for the sacrificing priest, see 1065; so 952, 3; --see also adv. dakṣiṇā. [√dakṣ: cf. δεξιός, Lat. dexter, ‘clever, right’; Goth. taihsva, ‘right hand’: from dakṣiṇa in mg 3, comes Deccan, name of the country south of Hindustan, lit. ‘the South.’]
दक्षिणा: dakṣiṇā́, adv. southerly; toward the south. [dákṣiṇa: acct, 1112e.]
दक्षिणाग्नि: dakṣiṇāgní, m. the southern fire, 1032, cf. 1022N.
दक्षिणाप्रवण: dakṣiṇā́-pravaṇa, a. sloping to the south. [dakṣiṇā, adv.]
दक्षिणायन: dakṣiṇāyana, n. south-course (of the sun), or the half-year from the summer to the winter solstice. [dakṣiṇa + ayana.]
दक्षिणारण्य: dakṣiṇāraṇya, n. the southern forest (a forest in the Deecan). [dakṣiṇa + araṇya.]
दक्षिणावत्: dákṣiṇāvant, a. abounding in gifts to the priests, i. e. (from the point of view of the priests) pious. [dákṣiṇā: see dakṣiṇa 5.]
दक्षिणावन्त्: dákṣiṇāvant, a. abounding in gifts to the priests, i. e. (from the point of view of the priests) pious. [dákṣiṇā: see dakṣiṇa 5.]
दग्ध: dagdhá, a. 	—1. burned; 	—2. pained, tortured; 	—3. wretched, good-for-nothing, cursed, damned. [ppl. of √dah: for mg 2, cf. √śuc.]
दग्धोदर: dagdhodara, n. one's cursed belly. [dagdha + udara.]
दण्ड: daṇḍá, m. stick; staff (of Brahman), 5923; mace, 978; rod as symbol of dominion and punishment. [cf. δένδρον, ‘tree.’]
दण्डभय: daṇḍa-bhaya, m. fear of the rod.
दण्डिन्: daṇḍín, a. bearing a staff; as m. warder. [daṇḍa.]
दत्त: dattá, a. given; as m. (a son) given (by his parents to others for adoption); common at end of proper names, esp. of Vaiśyas. [ppl. of √1dā, 955c.]
ददृह्: dadṛh, a. firm; dadhṛ́k, acc. s. n., as adv. firmly. [√dṛh.]
दधन्: dadhán [431], n. sour milk; curds. [orig., perhaps, ‘milk,’ fr. √2dhā.]
दधिकर्ण: dadhi-karṇa, m. Curd-ear, name of a cat. [‘having curd-ears, i. e. ears as white as curds.’]
दत्: dánt [396], m. tooth. [cf. ὀδόντα, Lat. dentem, Goth. tunϸus, AS. tōð, Eng. tooth, Old High Ger. zand, Ger. Zahn, ‘tooth.’]
दन्त्: dánt [396], m. tooth. [cf. ὀδόντα, Lat. dentem, Goth. tunϸus, AS. tōð, Eng. tooth, Old High Ger. zand, Ger. Zahn, ‘tooth.’]
दभ्: √dabh or dambh (dábhati; dadā́bha, dadámbha, debhús; ádabhat; dabdhá; dábdhum). harm with guile; hurt; deceive.
दम्: √dam (dā́myati [763]; dāntá [955a]; damitvā́; -dámya; damáyati). 	—1. he tame; 	—2. tame; conquer; become master;  control. [cf. δαμάω, Lat. domāre, ‘tame’; Eng. tame, Ger. zahm, ‘tame.’]
dám, n. house. [cf. δῶ, ‘house’: see under dáma.]
दम: dáma, m. n. house, home. [cf. δόμος, Lat. domus, ‘house, home’: it is not certain whether dáma comes from √dam and so means lit. ‘the place where one is master,  one's Gebiet,’ or whether it is to be connected w. δέμω, ‘build’: in the latter case, it would mean lit., like Ger. Bau, ‘a building,’ and should be connected w. AS. timber, *tem-ra, ‘building-material, a building, ’ Eng. timber, ‘building-material,’ Ger. Zimmer, ‘building-material, a building, a room.’]
damá, 	—1. a. conquering, at end of cpds; as m. 	—2. Dama, i. e. Victor, name of a son of Bhīma; 	—3. self-control. [√dam: cf. Ἱππό-δαμος, ‘Horse-tamer,’ etc.]
दमन: damana, 	—1. a. conquering, at end of cpds; 	—2. as m. Damana, i. e. Vincent, name of a priestly sage, and of a son of Bhīma. [√dam: cf. Lat. dominus, ‘master.’]
दमयन्ती: damayantī, f. Damayantī, i. e. Victoria, name of Bhīma's daughter. [‘conquering (men),’ fr. √dam, 1043. 5.]
दम्पति: dám-pati, m. master of the house; as dual, master and mistress, man and wife; pair. [acct, 1267a.]
दय्: √day (dáyate; dayā́m āsa; dayitá). 	—1. part; allot; 	—2. take part in; sympathize with; have tender feeling for; love; --dayita, loved, dear; as f., -tā, wife. [for 1, cf. κρέα δαίετο,, ‘parted, carved the meat’; for 2, cf. δαίεται ἦτορ, ‘heart is divided or takes part in (?), i. e. sympathizes.’]
दरिद्र: daridra, a. wandering about; mendicant; poor; as m. poor man. [fr. intens. of √1drā, ‘run about,’ 1147b2: for mg, cf. Eng. tramp, in its American sense of ‘vagrant beggar.’]
दर्प: darpa, m. wildness; wantonness; impudence;  pride. [√dṛp.]
दर्भ: darbhá, m. grass-tuft; grass used at sacrificial ceremonies, esp. Kuśa-grass, Poa cynosuroides. [√dṛbh.]
दर्श: darśa, m. sight; the moon when just becoming visible; the new moon; the day or festival of new moon. [√dṛś.]
दर्शक: darśaka, a. 	—1. seeing; 	—2. (fr. caus.) showing, making clear. [dṛś.]
दर्शत: darśatá, a. to be seen; visible. [√dṛś, 1176c.]
दर्शन: dárśana, a. seeing; as n. the beholding, sight; the becoming visible, 10320; appearance,  410. [√dṛś.]
दर्शपूर्णमास: darśa-pūrṇa-māsá, dual m. new and full moon; the days and the festivals of new and full moon.
दश: dáśa [4834], num. ten. [cf. δέκα, Lat. decem, Goth. taihun, Eng. ten, Ger. zehn, ‘ten’; Eng. -teen in six-teen, etc.]
दशम: daśamá, f. -ī́, a. tenth; daśamī́, sc. tithi, tenth day of a lunar half-month. [daśa, 4876.]
दशशत: daśa-śata, n. ten hundred; a thousand.
दशशाख: dáśaśākha, a. having ten branches, i. e. fingers. [dáśa + śā́khā: acct, 1300a.]
दशा: daśā, f. the threads projecting at the end of a weft, fringe; lamp-wick; fig. wick of life, course of life; time of life.
दशाह: daśāhá, m. space of ten days. [dáśa + 2 áha, 13124.]
दस्: √das (dásyati; dadā́sa; ádasat; dastá; dāsáyati). suffer lack. [cf. √dās, dasyu: also δέω, ‘lack.’] + vi, become exhausted.
दस्यु: dásyu, m. demon, foe of gods and men. [cf. √das, dāsá.]
दह्: √dah (dáhati, -te; dadā́ha, dehé; ádhākṣīt; dhakṣyáti; dagdhá; dágdhum; dagdhvā́; -dáhya; dahyáte). 	—1. burn with fire; burn; 	—2. pass.: be burned; be pained or tortured; 	—3. dagdha, see s. v. [for *dhagh: cf. Goth. dags, AS. dœg, Eng. day, Old High Ger. tak, ‘day.’] + ā, in ādahana. + vi, injure by burning, 8417. + sam, consume.
दा: √1dā (dádāti, dádati [668]; dadaú, dadé; ádāt, ádita [884]; dāsyáti, -te; dattá [955c], -tta [1087c]; dā́tum; dattvā́; -dā́ya; dīyáte [770b]; dítsati [1030]; dāpáyati). give; bestow; grant; impart; w. acc. of thing and dat. or gen., later also loc., of person, 117, 2320, 2117; varaṃ dā, grant a wish; śāpaṃ dā, (give, i. e.) pronounce a curse; saubhāgyaṃ dā, (give, i. e.) wish conjugal felicity; dā, (give, i. e.) sell, w. instr. of price, 474; uttaraṃ dā, make answer; śrāddhaṃ dā, perform a śrāddha, 443, 10417; punar dā, give back; --desid. desire or be ready to give. [cf. δίδωμι, Lat. dă-re, ‘give.’] + anu, (like Ger. nach-geben, ‘yield,’ and so) grant, admit; ppl. ánutta [1087e], admitted. + ā, take (opp. of give), 2817; grasp, 706; ādāya, having taken, equiv. to with. + upa_ā, receive, appropriate. + pari, deliver over; commit; entrust. + pra, give; grant; impart (sciences); ppl. f. práttā [1087e], given in marriage, married.

√2dā (dyáti [761d 3]; dadé; ádāt, ádita [884]; diná [957a], -tta [1087e]; -dā́ya; dīyáte). cut. [cf. √day, dāya.] + ava, cut off, esp. a part of the sacrificial cake; ppl. avatta [1087e], as subst. that which is cut off. + sam-ava, cut in pieces and collect them; ppl. samávatta, as subst. gathered pieces.
दातृ: dātṛ, m. giver; as a. [3753], generous, 214, 482. [√1dā.]
दान: dā́na, n. giving, imparting; gift. [√1dā, 1150: cf. Lat. dōnum, ‘gift.’]
दानधर्म: dāna-dharma, m. the virtuous practice of alms-giving.
दानव: dānavá, m. child of Dānu, a Dānava, one of a class of demons, foes of the gods; Titan. [1dā́nu, 1208c.]
दानु: 1dā́nu, f. Dānu, name of a demon, 7018.
दान्त: dānta, a. tamed, mild; subdued (as to one's passions); as subst. Dānta, name of a son of Bhīma. [ppl. of √dam, 955a.]
दाय: 2dāyá, m. portion, inheritance. [√2dā: cf. δαίς, ‘portion, meal.’]
दारु: dā́ru, n. wood; log or billet of wood; stick. [see the equiv. drú and taru: cf. δόρυ, ‘wood, beam, shaft’; δρῦς, ‘tree, oak’; Goth. triu, ‘wood, tree’; Eng. tree, ‘wood’ (so Wyclif), ‘a large woody plant’ (usual mg), ‘a wooden bar’ (in whiffle-tree).]
दाश्: √dāś (dā́śati; dadā́śa, dāśvā́ṃs [790b]). grant, offer; esp. serve or honor a god with offerings; dāśvā́ṃs, as subst. a pious servant of a god, 6911. [w. dadā́śa, cf. δέδωκα, ‘granted, gave’; ἔ-δωκ-α is an imperfect indicative without thematic vowel, corresponding to *á-dāś-am; but both Greek forms became connected in the popular mind with δίδωμι, ‘give.’]
दास्: √dās (only with abhi, abhidā́sati). bear ill-will to; try to harm. [cf. √das, dasyu, dāsa.]
दास: dāsá, m. 	—1. foe; esp. supernatural foe, evil demon; 	—2. (in opp. to ārya) foe of the gods, infidel; used like Caffre and Giaour; 	—3. (subdued foe, i. e.) servant, slave, 792; --dāsī́, f. female slave. [√dās: cf. √das, dasyu.]
दासपत्नी: dāsá-patnī, a. f. having the demon for their master. [acct, 1251b, 1295.]
दिति: díti, f. Diti, name of a deity without definite character, a mere pendant to aditi as sura to asura, and formed by popular etymology as sura from asura. [see aditi and daitya.]
दिदृक्षु: didṛ́kṣu, a. desirous to see. [fr. desid. of √dṛś, 1178f: acct !]
दिद्यु: didyú, m. missile. [see √1dīv or dyū, and 1147b2.]
दिधिषु: didhiṣú, a. desirous to win; as m. suitor; husband; esp. second husband. [fr. desid. of √1dhā, 1178f, 1028d.]
दिन: dína, 	—1. perhaps adj. clear, in su-dína; 	—2. as n. day. [perhaps ppl. of √dī or di, ‘shine,’ w. shifted acct.]
दिनत्रय: dina-traya, n. day-triad, trīduum, space of three days.
दिव्: √div : there is no verbal root div in Sanskrit: cf. noun dív and √√1 and 2dīv or dīū.

dív [361d], m. 	—1. sky, heaven, e. g. 722; 	—1a. Heaven, personified as Father, e. g. RV. vi. 51. 5; 	—1b. duhitā́ divás, of the Dawn, daughter of the sky or of Heaven, 7516; 	—2. day, e. g. 708, 7913; 	—3. observe that dív is sometimes fem. in Veda, so 921, 8, RV. x. 125. 7. [w. gen. div-ás, cf. the genitives Διός, *Διϝ-ός, Lat. Jŏv-is, and AS. Tiw-es in Tiwes dœg, Eng. Tues-day: (Tiw corresponds to the old Germanic Tiu, no longer a god of the sky or bright day, but rather a god of battle or fighting, the chief occupation of our early forefathers:) w. nom. dyaús, cf. •Δϳηύς: w. voc. dyau11ṣ pítar, cf. Ζεῦ πάτερ, Lat Jū-piter, ‘Heaven Father’: w. dúhitar divas, cf. θύγατερ Διός, ἄμβροτ᾽Ἀθάνα, Oedipus Rex 159: cf. also δῖος, ‘heavenly’; Lat. nom. Diovi-s, ‘god of heaven,’ Jŏv-em, ‘Jove’; sub dio, ‘under the sky’; Eng. Tewes-ley, ‘Tiw's lea,’ a place in Surrey.]
दिव: divá, n. heaven; day, in divé-dive, day by day. [dív, 1209a.]
दिवा: dívā, adv. by day. [fr. the instr. div-ā́, w. shifted acct, 1112e.]
दिवौकस्: divaukas, m. caelicola, god. [‘having heaven as a dwelling’: diva + okas.]
दिश्: √diś (diśáti; didéśa; ádikṣat, ádiṣṭa [883]; dekṣyáti; diṣṭá; déṣṭum; -díśya; diśyáte; deśáyati). point; direct; show. [cf. δείκνυμι, ‘show’; Lat. dīco, ‘show, tell’; AS. tāh, Ger. zieh, ‘pointed out (as guilty), accused’; Ger. zeigen, ‘show’; also AS. tāh-te, tǣh-te, Eng. taught, ‘showed, instructed’; AS. tācn, Eng. token.] + apa, show; make a false show of. + vy-apa, make a false show of. + ā, point out to, give a direction to, direct. + sam-ā, point out to, direct; command. + ud, point out; aim towards; uddiśya, w. acc., with an aiming towards, equiv. to the prep. at, 2622. + upa, show to, teach, instruct; give advice to, advise. + pra, point out, designate; direct.
díś, f. just like Eng. point, i. e. cardinal point, quarter of the heaven (N., E., S., W.); aṣṭau diśas, eight regions (N., E., S., W., and NE., SE., SW., NW.), 5712. [√diś, ‘to point.’]
दिह्: √dih (dégdhi; didihé; digdhá; -díhya). 	—1. stroke, touch lightly; 	—2. smear; 	—3. besmear, pollute. [for *dhigh: cf. ἔθιγον, ‘touched’; Lat. fingo, ‘form, fashion,  esp. with the hand in soft material’; Goth. daigs, ‘moulded mass of clay or bread-paste’; Old Eng. dāg, Eng. dough.] + sam, pass. (be plastered together, be indistinct, and so) be uncertain, doubtful.
दीक्ष्: √dīkṣ (dī́kṣate; didī́kṣa, didīkṣé; ádīkṣiṣṭa; dīkṣiṣyáte; dīkṣitá; dīkṣitvā́; -dī́kṣya). consecrate one's self, esp. for performing the Soma-sacrifice. [perhaps desid. of √dakṣ, ‘make one's self suitable or ready’: 108g.]
दीति: dīti, f. glance, flame, actually occurring only in su-dītí. [√dī, 1157. 1a.]
दीन: dīná, a. scanty; cast down, sad; wretched.
दीनार: dīnāra, m. denarius, name of a certain gold coin. [borrowed fr. Lat. dēnārius, a silver coin worth ten asses.]
दीप्: √dīp (dī́pyate; didīpé; dīptá; -dī́pya; dédīpti; dīpáyati, -te). blaze; flame; caus. kindle; intens. blaze brightly; fig. be radiant. [cf. √dī.] + ud, blaze up; caus. cause to blaze up.
दीर्घ: dīrghá, a. long, in space and in time; -am, as adv.; --comp. drā́ghīyāṃs, superl. drā́ghiṣṭha. [√drāgh: cf. δολιχός, ‘long.’]
दीर्घकर्ण: dīrgha-karṇa, m. Long-ear, name of a cat.
दीर्घराव: dīrgha-rāva, m. Long-yell or Far-howl, name of a jackal. (Their howling is both long-continued and far-reaching.)
दीर्घवर्णान्त: dīrghavarṇānta, a. having a long vowel as final. [anta.]
दीव्: √1dīv (dī́vyati; didéva [2403]; ádevīt; deviṣyáti; dyūtá; dévitum; -dī́vya). dice; play. [prop. dīū, see 7651 and 2: orig., perhaps, ‘throw,’ cf. didyu.] + ā, in ādevana.
√2dīv (dévati [2403]; dyūná [957a]; dévitum; deváyati, -te). lament. [prop. dīū, see 7651 and2.] + pari, moan, bemoan; caus. the same.
दुःख: duḥkhá, a. miserable; as n. misery, pain, sorrow. [cf. sukha.]
दुच्छुना: ducchúnā, f. calamity; harm. [dus + śuna, ‘mis-fortune, ill-luck,’ 1683.]
दुर्: dur-, the form taken by dus before sonants.
दुरतिक्रम: dur-atikrama, a. hard to overcome. [‘having a hard conquest,’ cf. 1304b.]
दुर्ग: dur-gá, a. whose going is hard, hard to go through or to, impassable; as n. difficult place; danger.
दुर्दान्त: dur-dānta, a. overcome with difficulty; as m. Hard-to-tame (Δυσνίκητος), name of a lion.
दुर्निवार: dur-nivāra, a. whose warding-off is hard; hard to get rid of.
दुर्बल: dur-bala, a. of (poor, i. e.) little strength; feeble.
दुर्बुद्धि: durbuddhi, a. of (bad, i. e.) small wit; foolish.
दुर्भग: dur-bhága, a. ill-portioned, ill-favored; -ā, f. ugly woman. [acct, 1304b.]
दुर्भिक्ष: dur-bhikṣa, a. (time) having its alms-getting hard, i. e. in which alms-getting is hard; as n. famine. [bhikṣā.]
दुर्मङ्गल: dur-maṅgala, a. of bad luck, bringing bad luck.
दुर्विपाक: dur-vipāka, m. evil issue (of one's destiny).
दुर्वृत्त: dur-vṛtta, a. of evil life, wicked.
दुवस्: duvás, n. perhaps same as dúvas, but see 7410N.
दुवस्य: √duvasya (duvasyáti). reward with a gift; honor or worship (a god) with an offering. [dúvas.] + ā, perhaps bring or entice hither by worship, but see 7410N.
दुष्कर: duṣ-kara, a. whose performance is hard, hard to be performed. [dus.]
दुष्ट: duṣṭa, a. spoiled; bad, morally; cross. [ppl. of √duṣ.]
दुस्: dus, inseparable prefix, characterizing a thing as evil, bad, hard; forming w. action-nouns cpds w. the same mg as if compounded w. a future pass. ppl., e. g. duṣ-kara, ‘having its doing hard, i. e. difficult to be done.’ [cf. √duṣ: also δυς-, ‘mis-’. see 2252.]
दुस्तर: dus-tara, a. having its crossing hard, hard to cross.
दुह्: √duh (dógdhi, dugdhé; dudóha, duduhé; ádhukṣat, -ata [918]; dhokṣyáte; dugdhá; dógdhum; dugdhvā́; doháyati). 	—1. milk; then, generalized 	—2. get the good out of a thing; 	—3. extract; 	—4. give milk; 	—5. in general, give or yield any good thing, 8016; --caus., like simple, milk, extract. [for mg 2, cf. ἀμέλγεσθαί τινα, ‘milk a person dry.’] + nis, milk out of; extract from.
दुहितृ: duhitṛ́ [3733], f. daughter. [derivation uncertain, 1182d: cf. θυγάτηρ, Goth. dauhtar, Eng. daughter, Ger. Tochter, ‘daughter. ’]
दू: √1dū, subsidiary form of √1dā, in dúvas, duvasya. [cf. √√sthā and gā w. their equiv. collateral forms sthū and gū.]
√2dū, go to a distance, in dūtá and dūrá. [cf. δεύομαι, ‘am at a distance from something,  fall short of.’]
दूडभ: dūḍábha, a. hard to deceive. [‘whose deceiving is hard’: for duzdabha, i. e. dus + dabha, 199b3.]
दूर: dūrá, a. far; as n. the distance; --caseforms as adverbs: -am, to a distance, far away; -e, in the distance, afar; at or from a distance; -āt, from afar. [√2dū, 1188.]
दूरीकृ: dūrī-kṛ (dūrīkaroti). put far away; send off. [dūra, 1094.]
दृ: √1dṛ (dṛṇā́ti; dadā́ra, dadré; ádārṣīt; dīrṇá; -dī́rya; dīryáte; dárdarti [1002b]; daráyati, dāráyati). burst, trans. and intrans.; --caus. and intens.: split; tear, w. gen. [cf. δέρω, δείρω, ‘flay’; AS. teran, Eng. tear, Ger. zerren, ‘tear, rend.’]

√2dṛ (driyáte; ádṛta; dṛtá; -dṛ́tya). used only w. ā, see 773. [cf. √δελ in δεν-δίλλω, ‘glance at’; AS. tilian, 'be intent upon, attend to, esp. the earth, i. e. till (the soil),’ Eng. till; Ger. zielen, ‘aim at’; AS. eorð-tilia, ‘earth-tiller.’] + ā, (look at, i. e.) regard; pass. be regarded,  i. e. respected.
दृति: dṛ́ti, m. bag of leather; bellows. [√1dṛ: for mg, cf. δέρμα, ‘skin bag or bottle.’]
दृप्: √dṛp (dṛ́pyati; ádṛpat; darpiṣyáti, drapsyáti; dṛptá; darpáyati). be crazed, wild, proud, insolent, or arrogant.
दृश्: √dṛś (dadárśa, dadṛśé; ádrākṣīt, ádṛṣṭa; drakṣyáti, -te; dṛṣṭá; dráṣṭum; dṛṣṭvā́; -dṛ́śya; dṛśyáte; dídṛkṣate; darśáyati). see; behold; --pass. be seen; be or become visible; appear; --caus. cause (a person, acc., 333) to see (a thing, acc., 336, 357, 367); show (w. gen. 632); w. ātmānam, show one's self, appear, pretend to be (e. g. frightened, 414). [present forms supplied by √1paś, q. v.: w. dadárśa, cf. δέδορκε, ‘saw’: cf. Goth. ga-tarh-jan, ‘make a show of.’] + prati, pass. appear over against one or before one's eyes. + vi, pass. be seen far and wide. + sam, behold; caus. show; w. ātmānam, show one's self, appear, pretend to be (e. g. dead).
dṛ́ś [2183, dṛk, dṛśam, dṛgbhyām], 	—1. vbl. seeing, looking; --2. as f. the seeing; dṛśé, as inf. [970a], for beholding; --3. in cpds [518], look, appearance. [√dṛś.]
दृश: dṛśa, m. the seeing; in cpds [518], look, appearance. [do.]
दृशि: dṛśí, f. the seeing; dṛśáye, as inf. [970f], for beholding. [do.]
दृश्य: dṛ́śya, grdv. to be seen; worthy to be seen, splendid. [√dṛś, 963d.]
दृषद्: dṛṣád, f. stone; esp. nether mill-stone.
दृषदुपला: dṛṣad-upalā́, dual f. the nether and the upper mill-stone. [1253a, 1258.]
दृष्टपूर्व: dṛṣṭa-pūrva, a. seen previously. [equiv. to pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭa, see 1291.]
दृष्टि: dṛ́ṣṭi, f. 	—1. seeing; 	—2. sense of sight; 	—3. glance, look; 	—4. view. [√dṛś: cf. δέρξις, ‘sense of sight.’]
दृह्: √dṛh (dṛ́ṃhati, -te [mg 1, cf. 758]; dṛ́hyati, -te [mg 2, see 767]; ádṛṃhīt; dṛḍhá [224a]; dṛṃháyati). 	—1. act. make firm or steady or enduring; establish; mid. be firm; dṛḍhá [1176a], firm; 	—2. be firm; 	—3. caus. make stable. [cf. Old Lat. forc-tis, Lat. fortis, ‘strong.’]
देय: déya, grdv. to be given or granted. [√dā, 963a.]
देव: devá, f. devī́, 	—1. a. heavenly, 7414, 16, 18, 927; as subst. 	—2. god, goddess; 	—2a. pl. the gods (in later times reckoned as 33, cf. tridaśa); 	—2b. víśve devā́s, all the gods; also all-gods (a term comprehending into a class all the separate gods, cf. All-saints, and see viśvádeva); 	—2c. devī́, The Goddess,  i. e. Śiva's wife, Durgā; 	—2d. -deva, at end of Brahman-names, having…as god, so, e. g., guṇadeva; --3. m. manuṣya-deva, god among men, i. e. a Brahman, see 951; similarly, 	—4. m. king, 1912, 504, 514, 7, 14; so used of a lion (3215) or even of a jackal (3621); f. queen. [perhaps fr. the noun dív (1209i): cf. Lat. deus, ‘god’: the alleged root div, ‘shine,’ has no existence.]
देवकाम: devá-kāma, a. having love for the gods. [acct, 12932, 1295.]
देवता: devátā, f. godhead or divinity, both as abstract and as concrete; devátā, instr., with divinity (collective), i. e. among deities, 7320 [1237.]
देवदूत: deva-dūtá, m. messenger of the gods.
देवदैवत्य: deva-daivatya, a. having the gods as divinity, (of hymns) addressed to the gods.
देवपति: deva-pati, m. lord of the gods, i. e. Indra.
देवपान: deva-pā́na, a. serving the gods for drinking. [lit. ‘god-drenching, i. e. gotttränkend’: acct, 1271, 1251c.]
देवयान: deva-yā́na, n. path of the gods, on which the intercourse between gods and men takes place. [acct, 1271, 1251c.]
देवराज: deva-rājá, m. king of the gods, i. e. Indra. [rājan, 1315a.]
देवलिङ्ग: deva-liṅga, n. god-characteristic, mark by which a god may be distinguished from a man.
देवशर्मन्: deva-śarman, m. Devaśarman or God'sjoy,  name of a certain Brahman. [of like mg is θεό-χαρις.]
देवसंनिधि: deva-saṃnidhi, m. presence of the gods.
देवहूति: devá-hūti, f. invocation of the gods. [acct, 1274.]
देवीकोट्ट: devī-koṭṭa, m. Goddess-fort, name of a town.
देवीविनिर्मित: devī-vinirmita, a. laid out by Durgā. [√1mā.]
देवृ: devṛ́ [3692], m. husband's brother. [cf. δαήρ, Lat. lēvir, ‘husband's brother.’]
देश: deśá, m. 	—1. (point, i. e.) place, 4118; 	—2. country, 245, see 9816N.; 	—3. place, pregnantly, as in Eng., i. e. proper place, 225; 	—4. as in Eng., place or region of the body, see muṣka-, skandha-. [√diś, ‘point.’]
देशभाषा: deśa-bhāṣā, f. dialect of the country.
देष्टृ: deṣṭṛ, m. pointer, guide, instructor; f. déṣṭrī, Instructress, as a deity, 909. [√diś, 1182: cf. *δεικτηρ in δεικτήριος, ‘pertaining to one who shows.’]
देह: deha, m. n. body; mentioned w. manas and vāc, 659. [√dih, ‘stroke lightly so as to mould or form,’ and so, prob. ‘the figure, form, shape,’ like the Lat. figūra, ‘shape, form,’ from the cognate √fig, fingo: see √dih.]
देहिन्: dehin, a. connected with the body, 6511; as m. a living being, man. [deha, 1230.]
दैत्य: daitya, m. descendant of Diti, q. v.; a Daitya or demon. [díti, 1211.]
दैत्यदानवमर्दन: daitya-dānava-mardana, m. Daitya-andDānava-crusher,  epithet of Indra.
दैव: daiva, a. of the gods, 5721; coming from the gods; divine; as n. divine appointment,  i. e. fate, 1812, etc. [devá, 1208f.]
दैवत: daivata, a. pertaining to a divinity; as n. 	—1. a divinity or, collectively, the divinities,  esp. that or those celebrated in any Vedic hymn; 	—2. idol, 6218. [devatā, 1208e.]
दैवत्य: daivatya, at end of cpds, having…as divinity, addressed to…, 635. [devatā, 1211.]
दैविक: daivika, a. of the gods; divine. [deva, 1222e.]
दैव्य: daívya, a. of the gods; divine. [devá, 1211.]
दोल: dola, m. a swinging; f. dolā, a dooly (Anglo-Indian term), a little bamboo chair slung on four men's shoulders. [√dul.]
दोलायमानमति: dolāyamāna-mati, a. having a wavering mind. [√dolāya.]
दोष: 1doṣa, m. 	—1. fault, defect; bad condition,  555; 	—2. sin, transgression, fault, 118, 1817, 6521; doṣam avāp, incur a transgression, 684; 	—3. harm; evil consequence;  doṣeṇa, doṣāt, by or as a bad consequence of, by, faute de, 2321, 352. [√duṣ.]
2doṣa, m. evening, dark; f. dosā́, evening, dark.
दोषावस्तृ: doṣā-vastṛ, m. illuminer of the darkness;  or, as adj. [cf. 3753], lighting up in the dark.
द्यावापृथिवी: dyā́vā-pṛthivī́, dual f. heaven and earth. [dív + pṛthivī́, 1255 and a2.]
द्युत्: √dyut (dyótate; didyuté; ádyutat; dyotiṣyáti; dyuttá; -dyútya). gleam; lighten; shine. [akin w. noun dív, q. v.: cf. also √jyut.] + vi, lighten.
द्रविण: dráviṇa, n. movable property (as opp. to house and field), wealth. [√dru, 1177b.]
द्रव्य: dravya, n. 	—1. property; 	—2. in general, thing, object; 	—3. esp. worthy object. [√dru: see draviṇa.]
द्रा: √1drā (drā́ti; dadraú; ádrāsīt; intens. [1002c, 10242] daridrāti). run; intens. run about, run hither and thither. [cf. δι-δρά-σκω, ‘run’: see √dru.] + apa, run off. [cf. ἀπο-δρᾶναι, ‘run off.’]
√2drā (drā́ti; drā́yate; dadraú; ádrāsīt; drāsyáti; drāṇá). sleep. [cf. ἔδραθον, ‘slept’; Lat. dormīre, ‘sleep.’] + ni, go to sleep; sleep.
द्राघ्: √drāgh, only in derivs. drag, draw; draw out; extend; lengthen. [poss. for *dhragh (cf. √dhraj), and akin w. Eng. drag: but see dīrghá.]
द्राघीयांस्: drā́ghīyāṃs, a. longer, as comp. to dīrghá. [√drāgh, 467.]
द्रु: √dru (drávati, -te; dudrā́va, dudruvé; ádudruvat [868]; droṣyáti; drutá; drótum; drutvā́; -drútya). hasten; run; run away, flee, 947. [ident. w. √dram, ‘run,’ and w. √1drā, q. v.: cf. ἔδρᾰμε and ἔδρᾱ, ‘ran.’] + ati, run past or by; escape. + ā, run unto, make an attack, charge, 945, 6. + upa, run unto. + sam-upa, run unto, rush at, 312.
द्रुत: druta, ppl. having hastened [9522]; -am, as adv. hastily, rapidly; quickly; immediately.  [√dru.]
द्रुम: druma, m. tree. [drú: cf. δρῡμός, ‘a wood.’]
द्रुह्: √druh (drúhyati; dudróha; ádruhat; dhrokṣyáti; drugdhá; drógdhum; -drúhya ). hurt (by deceit, wile, magic); strive to harm; ppl. drugdhá: as m. one who has striven to harm, hurtful foe; as n. misdeed. [if for *dhrugh, cf. Old High Ger. triukan, Ger. be-trügen, ‘deceive so as to harm.’] + abhi, offend against.
द्व: dvá [482b], num. two. [cf. δύο, Lat. duo, Eng. two.]
द्वन्द्व: dvaṃdvá, n. pair; quarrel. [dvaṃ-dvam is the repeated nom. s. n. of dva: cf. 12522.]
द्वंद्व: dvaṃdvá, n. pair; quarrel. [dvaṃ-dvam is the repeated nom. s. n. of dva: cf. 12522.]
द्वय: dvayá, a. twofold; of two sorts; as n. couple, pair. [dvá: cf. δοιός, ‘double.’]
द्वादश: dvā́daśa [4834], cardinal. twelve. [dvá + dáśa, 4763: cf. δυώδεκα, Lat. duōdecim, ‘twelve.’]
dvādaśá, f. -ī́, ordinal. twelfth; dvādaśī́ (sc. tithi), twelfth day of a lunar half month, 599. [dvā́daśa, 4877.]
द्वादशरात्र: dvādaśa-rātra, n. space of twelve nights. [dvā́daśa + rātri, 1315b, 13123, 4.]
द्वादशसाहस्र: dvādaśasāhasra, a. consisting of twelve thousand. [dvādaśa-sahasra, 1204c.]
द्वार्: dvā́r [388c], f. door. [perhaps ‘the closure, ’ fr. √dvṛ, ‘close,’ for *dhvṛ: cf. θύρα, ‘door’; Lat. foris, nom. s., ‘door’; Eng. door.]
द्वारपक्ष: dvāra-pakṣa, m. side of the door.
द्वि: dvi, form of dva in composition and derivation. [4756.]
द्विज: dvi-já, a. twice-born; as m. member of one of the three upper castes, re-born by virtue of investiture (see √nī + upa), 602, 5820, 594, 627; in a narrower sense, a Brahman,  2114, 434, 559, 6416.
द्विजन्मन्: dvi-jánman, a. having double birth; as m. same as dvija; man of one of the three upper castes, 591. [acct, 1300c.]
द्विजाति: dvi-jāti, a. and as m. same as dvijanman; man of one of the three upper castes, 5919.
द्विजोत्तम: dvijottama, m. the highest of the twiceborn,  i. e. a Brahman. [dvija + uttama.]
द्विता: dvitā́, adv. just so; so also; equally.
द्विधा: dvídhā, adv. in two parts, in twain. [1104.]
द्विपद्: dvi-pád [391], a. having two feet; as m. the two-footed one, man, 162; as n. sing. that which is two-footed, collectively, men, 901, 3, 923. [cf. δίποδα, Lat. bipedem, ‘biped. ’]
द्विपद: dvi-pada, f. -ī, a. having (taken) two steps.
द्विप्रव्राजिन्: dvi-pravrājin, f. -nī, a. in f. going after two (men), unchaste, 9814.
द्विष्: √dviṣ (dvéṣṭi, dviṣṭé; didvéṣa; ádvikṣat, -ata; dviṣṭá; dvéṣṭum). hate; show hatred; be hostile. [cf. ὀ-δύσ-αντο, ‘became wroth,’ w. prothetic ο.]
dvíṣ, vbl. hating, in cpds; as f. hate; as m. concrete, hater, foe. [√dviṣ.]
द्विस्: dvís, adv. twice. [see dvi, dva: cf. δίς, Lat. bis, *dvis, ‘twice’: the radically cognate Eng. twice is a gen. form.]
द्वीपिन्: dvīpín, a. having islands or island-like spots; as m. leopard; tiger. [dvīpa.]
द्वेधा: dvedhā́, adv. in two, in two kinds. [for *dvayadhā, fr. dvaya, 11042.]
द्वेषस्: dvéṣas, n. hatred; concrete, hater, foe. [√dviṣ.]
